Ravento is relevant for specialized AI applications, intelligent document processing, and workflow automation. LeewayHertz offers capabilities relevant to real estate AI agents, valuation support, and document-heavy workflows. Before making a final selection, request comparable technical proposals and verify each company's relevant project experience. For enterprise buyers, the most important consideration is whether the development partner can build a reliable application that integrates with existing systems, uses property data appropriately, and meets measurable business requirements. The strongest AI-powered real estate applications combine relevant data, practical AI capabilities, secure software architecture, and continuous evaluation.

title: How Muse Works: An Introduction
author: spran wiki
summary: Openclaw was a huge turning point in AI, marking the start of Agentic AI. Honestly though, Openclaw was super overhyped. After trying it, it took me forever to get it set up, and even after that it broke often. Connecting Gmail, calendar, etc. felt impossible, and to be honest, Openclaw lost me more time than it saved. When I saw Muse being released, I was confident it was going to be the same, but after a week of using it, it genuinely stood out to me. The app has gone super viral, hitting number 1 on the app store. How Muse works The first part is the Agent itself: this is just an LLM being called with an API request + context. As you talk with Muse, it stores important details in its Soul.md (which defines personality) and its Memory.md (which records important info). The second thing is by far the coolest, and the fact that Meta gives the basic version away for free is even more insane. Muse can actually use a computer, each Muse agent gets its own virtual computer along with a browser. The next big feature with Muse is safety and ease. For other AI agents, you have to create and link APIs if you want to access things like Google Calendar. With Muse, you just click connect and an auth connects you. It stores your logins where the AI agent never sees them. The Muse UI explained Muse’s interface is clean and minimal, designed around a central chat window where you communicate with your agent. Here’s what you’ll see: Chat Interface - Pretty standard, this is where you talk with your agent Navigation - Quick access to the main chat and Settings (app and agent configuration). Connected Apps - Shows the apps you’ve authenticated (Gmail, Google Calendar, etc.). Overall, the UI is not that hard to navigate, I recommend just trying the app and you will have it down in a few days.

title: ChatGPT Ads Now Rewrite Your Ad Copy by Default
author: Yousif Alias
summary: What changed in ChatGPT Ads on October 30? As of Friday, October 30, OpenAI's ad system can rewrite your ChatGPT ad, translate it, resize the image and send the click to a different page on your site, all without you approving each version. The setting, called creative enhancements, is now on by default for new and existing campaigns, Search Engine Journal reported . OpenAI warned advertisers by email on October 20. The email said these ads "can run automatically without requiring you to review or approve each version," according to PPC Land , which reproduced it. OpenAI's help page on creative enhancements lists the four kinds of change, and Search Engine Roundtable confirmed on October 30 that the auto-enable went out in OpenAI's weekly advertiser email. How many businesses does this affect? More than 100,000 advertisers have now run ads on ChatGPT, up from about 20,000 in August, and the ads show to free and Go users in 89 countries. OpenAI shared those numbers in late October when it added 26 new markets, Thurrott reported . So the default flipped for a pool of advertisers that grew five times in about two months. If you set up a campaign this summer, haven't opened Ads Manager since and didn't opt out before the deadline, the system is now editing your ads. What exactly can OpenAI change in your ad? ChatGPT Ads can change four parts of your ad: your headline and description, the language, the image size, and the landing page URL. The system builds versions from the conversation the ad shows up in, your original ad and the content on your landing page. Versions can be made ahead of time or on the fly. What changes What it means for you Headline and description The words a lead read may not be the words you wrote. Language Your ad can run in a language your team doesn't speak. Image size Resized images. OpenAI hasn't said whether that includes cropping. Destination URL The click can land on a different page of your site than the one you picked. Search Engine Journal found gaps in OpenAI's own docs. Ads Manager doesn't show a preview of every version, and no report breaks out each enhanced version on its own. The help page also doesn't say how your tracking tags carry over when the system swaps the landing page. Why should a business owner who answers leads care? Your sales process starts with the promise in the ad. If software rewrote that promise, the person calling you or filling out your form may expect something you never offered. Your team won't know, because nobody on your side saw that version. I've been running ads since 2013, and one of the fastest ways to lose a good lead on the first call is a mismatch. The ad said one thing, the person who picks up says another, and the lead stops trusting both. Automated rewrites make that mismatch more likely, and you can't see it from Ads Manager. The landing page swap worries me more. If your form, your booking calendar or your tracking sits on one page and the system sends people to another, you can lose leads you paid for and never find out why. Should you keep creative enhancements on or turn them off? Test creative enhancements before you decide. Keep it on for one campaign and off for a matching one, run both for two to three weeks, and compare cost per booked appointment. OpenAI's own help page says changes over time do not, on their own, prove the feature worked. Open Ads Manager, go to Settings and check the creative enhancement toggle. Account settings are the default, and campaign settings override them. If you sell something regulated or price-sensitive (legal, medical, finance, anything with a specific offer or guarantee), turn it off. You need to approve every word. Add UTM tags to every destination URL so you can see which page leads actually landed on. Ask every new lead what they saw and write it in your CRM. It's the only way to catch a rewritten promise. Judge both campaigns on booked and closed deals. To compare the two campaigns on money in, run each one through our free ROAS calculator . A higher click-through rate means nothing if the leads from the rewritten ads don't buy. Where are ad platforms headed with AI creative? Ad platforms keep moving creative decisions from you to their AI and making that the default. ChatGPT now does it to every self-serve advertiser who didn't opt out. You control less of the ad than you used to. You still control what happens after the click: how fast you respond, whether the person answering knows what the lead was promised, and whether the booking sticks. Leads that wait go cold fast, which we break down in our speed to lead guide . Let your follow-up catch what the ad platform changes KenjiAI's Voice AI agents call or text a new lead within a minute, ask what brought them in, and log the answer in the CRM before booking. If an ad version is promising the wrong thing, you see it in a day instead of at the end of the month. We've run campaigns at 5x ROAS, and fast, consistent follow-up is a big part of how we got there. Next step: open ChatGPT Ads Manager today, check the toggle on every campaign, and add a "what did you see?" field to your lead intake before the next lead comes in. FAQ Are ChatGPT creative enhancements on by default? Yes. Since October 30, 2026, OpenAI turns creative enhancements on by default for new and existing self-serve ChatGPT Ads campaigns. Advertisers who opted out earlier keep their opt-out. How do I turn off creative enhancements in ChatGPT Ads? Go to Settings in ChatGPT Ads Manager and switch the creative enhancement toggle off. You can set it at the account level as a default and override it per campaign. The change only affects ads served from that point on. Can ChatGPT change the landing page of my ad? Yes. With creative enhancements on, OpenAI can send clicks to a different page on your website that it thinks fits the conversation better. OpenAI has not said how tracking parameters carry over or whether you can exclude pages, so tag every URL and watch where leads land. Do paying ChatGPT users see ads? No. Ads show only to people on the free and Go plans. Plus, Pro and Enterprise subscribers get an ad-free ChatGPT, so your ads reach the free and lower-priced tiers only. title: Check an options agent for early assignment and pin risk
author: Agent Risk Desk
summary: If your agent sells covered calls and put spreads, the order check at entry is the easy part. The two problems I care about show up later, while the position sits there: early assignment before an ex-dividend date, and pin risk on expiration day. Both are about the calendar. A covered call that looked fine when it was sold can get assigned the night before the stock goes ex-dividend. A short put that closes a few cents from its strike on Friday can turn into stock you only find out about on Saturday. Over the weekend I posted a short rundown of these risks . This one has the code and the actual responses. I run every open options position through options_risk_check each morning, and again on expiration day. The function import os , requests AFA = " https://agent-financial-advisor.agent-financial-advisor.workers.dev/v1/tools/options_risk_check " ACT_ON = { " early_assignment_dividend " , " pin_risk " } def options_check ( account , underlying , legs , as_of = None ): body = { " account " : account , " underlying " : underlying , " legs " : legs } if as_of : body [ " as_of " ] = as_of key = os . environ . get ( " AFA_API_KEY " ) headers = { " authorization " : f " Bearer { key } " } if key else {} r = requests . post ( AFA , json = body , headers = headers , timeout = 10 ) r . raise_for_status () result = r . json () flags = [ c for c in result [ " checks " ] if c [ " status " ] != " pass " and c [ " check " ] in ACT_ON ] return result , flags as_of defaults to today in New York. I pass it here so the examples below are reproducible. One thing to watch if you used my pre-trade check post: this tool names its fields check and detail . pre_trade_check uses id and message . Early assignment before a dividend Test account: margin, $40,000 equity, 200 shares of KO, short 2 KO Nov 20 70 calls. KO is at $72.40 and the call trades at $2.55. For the test I set the ex-dividend date to Nov 13 with a $0.53 dividend. Use the real date from your data feed. result , flags = options_check ( account = { " type " : " margin " , " equity " : 40000 , " cash " : 8000 , " options_level " : 2 , " shares_held " : 200 }, underlying = { " symbol " : " KO " , " price " : 72.40 , " ex_dividend_date " : " 2026-11-13 " , " dividend " : 0.53 }, legs = [{ " type " : " call " , " side " : " short " , " strike " : 70 , " expiry " : " 2026-11-20 " , " quantity " : 2 , " premium " : 2.55 }], as_of = " 2026-11-02 " , ) Here's what came back (trimmed): { "decision" : "approve_with_warnings" , "summary" : "APPROVE_WITH_WARNINGS: 0 failed, 1 warning(s), 4 passed." , "margin_requirement_usd" : 0 , "max_loss_usd" : 0 , "required_options_level" : 1 , "structures" : [ { "kind" : "covered_call" , "quantity" : 2 , "legs" : [ "short 2 KO 2026-11-20 70 calls" ], "requirement_usd" : 0 } ], "checks" : [ { "check" : "early_assignment_dividend" , "status" : "warn" , "detail" : "Short 70 call is in the money with $0.15 time value, less than the $0.53 dividend going ex on 2026-11-13. Expect assignment the day before; close or roll it if you don't want to deliver 200 shares and owe the dividend." , "source" : "OCC Rule 805(d); OCC Characteristics and Risks of Standardized Options" } ] } The math is simple. The call is $2.40 in the money, so only $0.15 of the $2.55 is time value. Whoever owns that call gets more from exercising and collecting the $0.53 dividend than from holding it. The position is still covered and the margin requirement is $0. Nothing is wrong with the trade itself. The agent just has to decide by the close on Nov 12 whether it wants to give up the shares. Pin risk on expiration day Second test account: margin, $25,000 equity, level 3. The position is a put spread on SPY, short 3 Nov 6 580 puts and long 3 Nov 6 575 puts. SPY is at $580.20. I ran the same legs twice. With as_of set to Wednesday, Nov 4, it came back approve with 4 checks passed. Max loss $1,155, requirement $1,500. There was no pin warning. With as_of set to Friday, Nov 6, the expiration day, it added this: { "check" : "pin_risk" , "status" : "warn" , "detail" : "Short 580 put expires 2026-11-06 with the stock within 1% of the strike. Whether you're assigned won't be known until after the close; close it to avoid an unplanned position over the weekend or overnight." , "source" : "OCC Rule 805(d); OCC Characteristics and Risks of Standardized Options" } This is the one that worries me with agents. The spread caps the loss at $1,155 only if both legs behave. If SPY closes at $579.90, the 575 long expires worthless and the 580 short can be assigned. That's 300 shares of SPY, about $174,000, in a $25,000 account over the weekend. An agent that only looks at max loss isnt going to see it coming. So on expiration morning the loop is short: for pos in open_positions : result , flags = options_check ( pos [ " account " ], pos [ " underlying " ], pos [ " legs " ]) for c in flags : print ( f " { pos [ ' underlying ' ][ ' symbol ' ] } { c [ ' check ' ] } : { c [ ' detail ' ] } " ) close_or_roll ( pos ) open_positions and close_or_roll are yours. I'd hand flagged positions to the agent with the detail text and let it pick between closing and rolling. A stricter setup would close them outright. Limits and setup No signup for the first 5 calls a day. POST /v1/keys gives a free key with 25 calls a day. Put it in AFA_API_KEY . It only knows what you send. The ex-dividend date and dividend come from your data, and so do the prices. The 1% pin band is a default. Pass pin_band_pct in the policy object to change it. Greeks come back as null unless you send delta , gamma , theta and vega on every leg. It's rule-based analysis for software, not investment advice. The same call also does margin under FINRA Rule 4210, cash-account limits, required options level and auto-exercise of expiring in-the-money longs. The docs and examples are in the repo: agent-financial-advisor . Over MCP the server is at https://agent-financial-advisor.agent-financial-advisor.workers.dev/mcp and the tool is options_risk_check . Disclosure: I built this. If your agent trades options and keeps getting surprised by something else, tell me in the comments.
